### 1. Workspace Initialization

This R Markdown document prepares the data and figures for the Climate 
Change Vulnerability Assessment for Logan Pass Water Supplies at Glacier 
National Park.

```{r setup}
# --- 1. Global Knitr Options ---
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE, 
  message = FALSE, 
  warning = FALSE, 
  eval = TRUE
)

# --- 2. Load Data and Dependencies ---
# Load site-specific datasets for GLAC
#load("data/park/GLAC/GLAC_data.RData")

# Source custom functions and libraries
source('setup.R')

# --- 3. Interactive Map Configuration ---
# Configure mapview defaults for standard Esri basemaps
mapviewOptions(
  fgb = FALSE, 
  georaster = FALSE, 
  basemaps = c("CartoDB.Positron", "Esri.WorldTopoMap", "Esri.WorldImagery")
)

# --- 4. Color Palettes ---
# Standard project palette
pal <- list(
  black     = "black", 
  gold      = "#dca237", 
  lightblue = "#6eb2e4", 
  teal      = "#459a74", 
  yellow    = "#eee461", 
  darkblue  = "#3070ad", 
  orange    = "#c66426", 
  pink      = "#c07da5",
  lightpink = "#ECD8E4"
)

# NPS-specific branding palette
nps_pal <- list(
  blue      = "#85b6dc", 
  red       = "#c5312a", 
  grey      = "#a9a9a9", 
  lightgrey = "#dcdcdc"
)

# --- 5. Hydrological Constants & Timeframes ---
# Unit conversions: Cubic Feet <-> Gallons
gal_to_cf <- 0.1336805
cf_to_gal <- 1 / gal_to_cf 

# Define analysis windows for comparison
hist_yrs <- c(1979, 2012)  # Historical reference period
fut_yrs  <- c(2035, 2065)  # Mid-century projection window
```

Building on the previous section, this chunk defines the spatial extent of the 
study and retrieves the necessary administrative and infrastructure layers from 
the NPS DataStore.

We define the primary study area using 4-digit NPS Unit Code 
(<https://www.nps.gov/aboutus/foia/upload/NPS-Unit-List.xlsx>) and retrieve 
spatial boundaries and building footprints.

```{r park_dat}
# --- 1. Define Study Unit ---
# Glacier National Park (GLAC)
park <- "GLAC"

# --- 2. Retrieve Administrative Boundaries ---
# Fetch park geometry and metadata from the NPS IRMA DataStore
park_boundary <- getParkBoundary(park = park)
state         <- park_boundary$STATE

# --- 3. Infrastructure and Hydrology ---
# Retrieve building footprints intersecting the park boundary
buildings <- getBuildings(park_boundary, dist = 0)

# Load the manually delineated recharge area
# Note: This KML represents the specific contributing area for 
# the Logan Pass system
recharge_area <- st_read("data/park/GLAC/logan_contrib_area.kml") %>%
  st_transform(crs = st_crs(park_boundary))

# Logan Pass supply and demand dataset from park
logan_sd <- read_csv("data/park/GLAC/logan_pass_supply_demand.csv") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(date = as.Date(date, format = "%m/%d/%y"),
                supply_gal = as.numeric(supply_gal),
                use_gal = as.numeric(use_gal)) %>%
  # a handful of days have recorded use a factor of 10 above preceeding and
  # following days. This volume is often 10x the tank capacity, and therefore
  # an implausible volume. Dividing by 10 clearly corrects the data to the
  # intended value. Given that these are manual measurements, these are
  # attributed to human-error and easily corrected. Note, all outlier values 
  # were triple confirmed to match the spreadsheet provided by the park. 
  dplyr::mutate(use_gal = ifelse(use_gal > quantile(use_gal, 0.99, na.rm = TRUE), 
                                 use_gal/10, use_gal))
# Summarize to monthly sum
logan_sd_monthly <- logan_sd %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ym = make_ym(date)) %>%
  group_by(ym) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    supply_gal = sum(supply_gal, na.rm = TRUE),
    use_gal = sum(use_gal, na.rm = TRUE),
    # Count rows where use_gal is not NA
    n_days_data = n(),
    # Calculate total days in that specific month/year
    days_in_month = days_in_month(first(ym))
  )

logan_sd_annual <- logan_sd %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year = year(date)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(year) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    avg_supply = mean(supply_gal, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_use    = mean(use_gal, na.rm = TRUE),
    # Find the middle of the x-axis for label placement (August)
    label_date = as.Date(paste0(unique(year), "-08-01")), 
    .groups = "drop"
  )

```


```{r use_demand_plot}

# 1. Calculate annual averages for lines and labels

# 2. Refined Plot
ggplot(logan_sd %>% dplyr::mutate(year = year(date)), aes(x = date)) +
  
  # Annual Average Horizontal Lines
  geom_hline(data = logan_sd_annual, aes(yintercept = avg_supply), 
             color = pal$darkblue, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(data = logan_sd_annual, aes(yintercept = avg_use), 
             color = pal$pink, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.6) +
  
  # Data Layers
  geom_line(aes(y = supply_gal, color = "Supply"), size = 0.7) +
  geom_point(aes(y = supply_gal, color = "Supply"), size = 1, shape = 21, fill = "white") +
  
  geom_line(aes(y = use_gal, color = "Use"), size = 0.7) +
  geom_point(aes(y = use_gal, color = "Use"), size = 1, shape = 21, fill = "white") +
  
  # Text Labels for Averages (formatted to thousands)
  geom_text(data = annual_stats, 
            aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, 
                label = paste0("Avg Supply: ", round(avg_supply/1000, 1), "k")),
            vjust = 1.3, hjust = 1.1, size = 3, color = pal$darkblue, fontface = "bold") +
  
  geom_text(data = annual_stats, 
            aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, 
                label = paste0("Avg Use: ", round(avg_use/1000, 1), "k")),
            vjust = 3, hjust = 1.1, size = 3, color = pal$pink, fontface = "bold") +
  
  # Formatting
  theme_bw() +
  scale_x_date(labels = date_format("%b"), date_breaks = "1 month") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x / 1000, "k")) + # Standardize to 'k'
  labs(x = "", y = "Gallons per Day") +
  scale_color_manual("", values = c("Supply" = pal$darkblue, "Use" = pal$pink)) +
  facet_wrap(~year, scales = "free_x", nrow = 2, ncol = 5) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.margin = margin(t = -20, b = 0, l = 0, r = 0))

ggsave("data/park/GLAC/Figs/logan_sd.jpg", dpi = 600, width = 7, height = 4)

```

### 2. Identify the water supplies

In this section, we extract the site-specific water supply information and delineate the hydrological boundaries for the Logan Pass system.

##### ---- Water Supply Database

We utilize a comprehensive National Park Service database to isolate water supply sources for the study unit and perform a spatial join to identify their respective watersheds. The database contains a row for each water supply system and source of water (e.g., individual wells, diversions, and springs) associated with each supply.

```{r}


# --- 1. Load and Clean Water Supply Database ---
table_path <- "data/Water_Supply_Systems/NPS_Water_Systems_Database_Joined.xlsx"

# Import database and convert to spatial (sf) object
WSD <- read_excel(table_path, sheet = 1, na = c("NA", "U"), skip = 1) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::filter(park_unit == park) %>%
  # Remove records missing spatial coordinates
  drop_na(c("source_longitude", "source_latitude")) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("source_longitude", "source_latitude"),
           crs = 4326, 
           remove = FALSE)

# --- 2. Target Site Selection ---
# Filter for Logan Pass infrastructure
select_sources <- WSD %>% 
  dplyr::filter(grepl("Logan", water_system_name))

# --- 3. Watershed Delineation ---
# Delineate watersheds for selected sources using point locations
select_sources <- select_sources %>%
  dplyr::mutate(watershed = purrr::map(
    .x = 1:nrow(.),
    .f = ~ getXYWatersheds(sf = select_sources[.x, ], 
                           coordinates = NULL, 
                           snap = TRUE)
  ))

# --- 4. Spatial Visualization: Park-Wide Systems ---
mapview(park_boundary,
        col.regions = "seagreen",
        alpha.regions = 0.2,
        color = "white",
        lwd = 3,
        layer.name = "Park Boundary") +
  mapview(WSD, 
          zcol = "source_type",
          layer.name = "All Water Sources") +
  mapview(select_sources,
          col.regions = "yellow",
          alpha.regions = 0,
          color = "yellow",
          lwd = 4,
          cex = 8,
          layer.name = "Selected Project Sources")

# --- 5. Spatial Visualization: Logan Pass Focus ---
# Filter buildings to those within 1km of the selected sources
sel_bldg <- buildings %>%
  st_filter(st_buffer(st_transform(select_sources, st_crs(buildings)), 1000))


# Plot all

mapview(select_sources$watershed,
        color = "dodgerblue",
        alpha.regions = 0.1,
        col.regions = "dodgerblue",
        lwd = 2,
        layer.name = "Auto-Delineated Rch. Area") +
  mapview(recharge_area,
        color = "navy",
        alpha.regions = 0.1,
        col.regions = "navy",
        lwd = 2,
        layer.name = "Manually-Delineated Rch. Area") +
  mapview(select_sources,
          col.regions = "yellow",
          alpha.regions = 1,
          color = "yellow",
          lwd = 4,
          cex = 8,
          layer.name = "Logan Pass Infiltration Gallery") +
  mapview(sel_bldg,
          col.regions = "gray40",
          layer.name = "Nearby Infrastructure")

```



#### ----- Weather stations

In this section, we retrieve historical climatological data from the NOAA Global Historical Climatology Network (GHCN) for stations within and surrounding Glacier National Park. The raw data is processed to standardize units and summarized into monthly and annual water-year aggregates.

This chunk handles the acquisition of GHCN weather station data, performs unit conversions for US customary standards (Inches and Fahrenheit), and calculates cumulative metrics for hydrological assessment.
```{r weather_stations}

# --- 1. Retrieve NOAA Weather Data ---
# Buffer park boundary by 5km to capture representative peripheral stations
noaa <- getNOAA(st_buffer(park_boundary, 5000), "GLAC") %>% 
  st_transform(4326)

# Extract a metadata list of unique stations
stations <- noaa %>%
  group_by(name) %>%
  slice(1) %>% 
  ungroup()

# --- 2. Data Cleaning and Unit Conversion ---
# GHCN data often scales values (e.g., Temp * 10); we revert these to standard units
weather_data <- noaa %>%
  dplyr::select(name, id, date, prcp, snow, snwd, tmax, tmin, tobs) %>%
  # Reconvert values stored as tenths (mm * 0.1 to mm, C * 0.1 to C)
  dplyr::mutate_at(c("tmax", "tmin", "prcp"), ~ .x * 0.10) %>%
  # Convert Millimeters to Inches
  dplyr::mutate_at(c("snow", "snwd", "prcp"), ~ .x * 0.0393701) %>%
  # Convert Celsius to Fahrenheit
  dplyr::mutate_at(c("tmax", "tmin"), ~ (9/5) * .x + 32)

# --- 3. Monthly Summaries and Accumulation ---
weather_data_mon <- weather_data %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ym = lubridate::ym(substr(date, 1, 7)),
                year = year(date)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ym, name, id) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(tmax  = max(tmax, na.rm = TRUE),
                   tmin  = min(tmin, na.rm = TRUE),
                   tmean = mean(c(tmax, tmin), na.rm = TRUE),
                   prcp  = sum(prcp, na.rm = TRUE),
                   snow  = sum(snow, na.rm = TRUE),
                   snwd  = max(snwd, na.rm = TRUE),
                   .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Date = ym) %>%
  addWaterYear() %>%
  dplyr::group_by(waterYear, name) %>%
  # Calculate cumulative metrics for water balance
  dplyr::mutate(prcp_cum = cumsum(prcp),
                snow_cum = cumsum(snow),
                snwd_cum = max(snwd, na.rm = TRUE),
                # Melt proxy: cumulative snowfall minus current snow depth
                melt = snow_cum - snwd) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

# --- 4. Annual Water Year Summaries ---
weather_data_an <- weather_data %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(waterYear = calc_water_year(date, water_year_start_month = 10)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(waterYear, name, id) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(tmax  = mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE),
                   tmin  = mean(tmin, na.rm = TRUE),
                   tmean = mean(c(tmax, tmin), na.rm = TRUE),
                   prcp  = sum(prcp, na.rm = TRUE),
                   snow  = sum(snow, na.rm = TRUE),
                   snwd  = max(snwd, na.rm = TRUE),
                   .groups = "drop")

# --- 5. Selection and Visualization ---
# Target stations with long-term reliable records for Logan Pass context
select_station_list <- c("USS0013A19S", "USS0013A27S")

# Map selected stations by elevation
mapview(stations %>% 
          dplyr::filter(id %in% select_station_list) %>%
          dplyr::mutate(elevation_ft = elevation / 0.3048), 
        zcol = "elevation_ft",
        layer.name = "Station Elevation (ft)") +
  mapview(select_sources,
          col.regions = "tomato",
          cex = 10,
          layer.name = "Water Sources")

# Plot annual trends for selected meteorological variables
ggplot(weather_data_an %>% 
         dplyr::filter(id %in% select_station_list) %>%
         pivot_longer(cols = c("tmax", "tmin", "tmean", "prcp", "snwd"),
                      names_to = "vars",
                      values_to = "vals"),
       aes(x = waterYear, y = vals, color = name)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(lwd = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~vars, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_color_colorblind("Station Name") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Water Year", y = "Value (Standard Units)")

# --- 6. Cleanup ---
rm(noaa, weather_data)
gc() # Force garbage collection to free memory


```

#### ----- SNOTEL

In this segment, we retrieve and process data from the SNOTEL (Snow Telemetry) network. SNOTEL stations provide critical high-elevation data, including Snow Water Equivalent (SWE), which is essential for understanding the timing and magnitude of snowmelt recharge at Logan Pass.

This chunk identifies SNOTEL stations within and near the park, tidies the sensor data (Precipitation, Snow Depth, and SWE), and calculates annual maximums for water-year trend analysis.


```{r snotel}

# --- 1. Retrieve SNOTEL Data ---
# Search for SNOTEL sites within a 3km buffer of the park boundary
snotel <- getSNOTEL(aoi = recharge_area %>%
                      dplyr::mutate(Name = "Recharge Area"), 
                    dist = 20000, 
                    years = "all") %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  st_transform(4326)

# Extract unique station metadata for mapping
snotel_sites <- snotel %>%
  group_by(site) %>%
  dplyr::slice(1) %>% 
  ungroup()

# --- 2. Spatial Visualization: Station Locations ---
mapview(park_boundary, 
        alpha.regions = 0.1, 
        layer.name = "Park Boundary") +
  mapview(select_sources, 
          col.regions = "red", 
          layer.name = "Water Sources") +
  mapview(snotel_sites, 
          col.regions = "darkblue", 
          layer.name = "SNOTEL Sites")

# --- 3. Tidy and Pivot Sensor Data ---
snotel_tidy <- snotel %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  # Filter for cumulative precip, snow depth, and snow water equivalent (SWE)
  dplyr::filter(sensor_id %in% c("PREC.I", "SNWD.I", "WTEQ.I")) %>%
  dplyr::select(date, station_name, value, sensor_id, water_year) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(date, station_name, sensor_id, water_year) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(value = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = sensor_id, values_from = value) %>% 
  clean_names() %>%
  # Convert precipitation from millimeters to inches
  dplyr::mutate(prec_mm = prec_i * 0.1, # scaling factor (assumed - need to confirm)
                prec_in = prec_mm * 0.0393701) 

# --- 4. Monthly and Annual Summarization ---
# Monthly aggregation for hydrological modeling
snotel_m <- snotel_tidy %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ym = lubridate::ym(substr(date, 1, 7))) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ym) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(snwd = max(snwd_i, na.rm = TRUE),
                   prec = sum(prec_in, na.rm = TRUE),
                   wteq = max(wteq_i, na.rm = TRUE))

# Annual aggregation for vulnerability assessment
snotel_annual <- snotel_tidy %>%
  dplyr::group_by(station_name, water_year) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(wteq = max(wteq_i, na.rm = TRUE),
                   prec = sum(prec_in, na.rm = TRUE),
                   snwd = max(snwd_i, na.rm = TRUE),
                   .groups = "drop")

# --- 5. Visualization: Annual SWE Trends ---

ggplot(snotel_annual, aes(x = water_year, 
                          y = wteq, 
                          color = station_name, 
                          fill = station_name)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.3, lwd = 0.8) +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_color_colorblind("SNOTEL Site") +
  scale_fill_colorblind("SNOTEL Site") +
  labs(title = "Annual Maximum Snow Water Equivalent (SWE)",
       x = "Water Year",
       y = "Max SWE (inches)") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

# --- 6. Memory Cleanup ---
rm(snotel)
gc()

```



#### ----- NWIS Surface Water

In this section, we analyze surface water dynamics using data from the USGS National Water Information System (NWIS). We focus on stream gages near Glacier National Park to establish baseline hydrological regimes and identify shifts in the timing and magnitude of peak snowmelt and baseflow discharge.

This chunk retrieves daily discharge data for relevant stream gages, summarizes hydrological patterns by Day of Year (DOY), and compares "early" vs. "late" historical periods alongside recent 2025 observations.


```{r nwis, eval = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# --- 1. Identify Nearby Stream Gages ---
# Define bounding box for the park unit
bbox_vals <- sf::st_bbox(park_boundary) %>%
  as.numeric() %>% 
  round(digits = 5)

# Retrieve monitoring locations and calculate distance to water sources
usgs_sw <- read_waterdata_monitoring_location(bbox = bbox_vals, site_type = "Stream") %>%
  st_transform(crs = st_crs(park_boundary)) %>%
  st_filter(park_boundary) %>%
  mutate(dist_m = as.numeric(st_distance(geometry, st_transform(select_sources, st_crs(park_boundary)))))

# Select the 15 nearest sites for initial screening
nearest_usgs_sw <- usgs_sw %>% 
  slice_min(order_by = dist_m, n = 15)

# --- 2. Retrieve Daily Discharge Data ---
usgs_discharge <- read_waterdata_daily(
  monitoring_location_id = nearest_usgs_sw$monitoring_location_id,
  parameter_code = "00060" # Discharge, cubic feet per second
)

# Refine station list based on successful data retrieval
nearest_usgs_sw <- nearest_usgs_sw %>%
  dplyr::filter(monitoring_location_id %in% unique(usgs_discharge$monitoring_location_id))

# Join station metadata to discharge records
usgs_discharge <- usgs_discharge %>%
  left_join(nearest_usgs_sw %>% st_drop_geometry() %>%
              dplyr::select(monitoring_location_id, monitoring_location_name, altitude, agency_code),
            by = "monitoring_location_id")

# --- 3. Process Hydrographs and Period Comparisons ---
# Clean location names for publication-quality labels
clean_names_fn <- function(df) {
  df %>% mutate(
    monitoring_location_name = gsub("nr. |nr ", "near ", monitoring_location_name),
    monitoring_location_name = gsub("C |Cr ", "Creek ", monitoring_location_name),
    monitoring_location_name = gsub("ab ", "above ", monitoring_location_name),
    monitoring_location_name = gsub("Lk ", "Lake ", monitoring_location_name),
    monitoring_location_name = gsub("G ", "Grinnell ", monitoring_location_name)
  )
}

# Define "Early" and "Late" historical record splits
usgs_discharge_doy <- usgs_discharge %>%
  dplyr::filter(year(time) > 1957) %>%
  clean_names_fn() %>%
  group_by(monitoring_location_name) %>%
  mutate(
    global_start = min(time),
    global_end = max(time),
    period = ifelse(time < global_start + (global_end - global_start) / 2, "early", "late")
  ) %>%
  group_by(doy = yday(time), monitoring_location_name, period) %>%
  summarize(
    p_start = min(time),
    p_end = max(time),
    discharge = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    discharge_min = min(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    discharge_max = max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(doy_date = as.Date(doy, origin = "2019-12-31"))


# --- 4. Identify 2025 Observations for Comparison ---
usgs_discharge_doy_2025 <- usgs_discharge %>%
  dplyr::filter(year(time) == 2025) %>%
  clean_names_fn() %>%
  group_by(doy = yday(time), monitoring_location_name) %>%
  summarize(
    discharge = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(doy_date = as.Date(doy, origin = "2019-12-31"),
         period = "2025")


# --- 5. Generate Labels and Visualization ---
facet_labels <- usgs_discharge_doy %>%
  group_by(monitoring_location_name, period) %>%
  summarize(p_min = min(p_start), p_max = max(p_end), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(period_string = paste0(period, ": ", format(p_min, "%Y"), "-", format(p_max, "%Y"))) %>%
  group_by(monitoring_location_name) %>%
  summarize(full_label = paste(period_string, collapse = "\n"),
            x_pos = as.Date("2020-01-01"), y_pos = Inf, .groups = "drop")

# --- 1. Faceted Hydrograph for All Stations ---
# This restoration includes all gages to show spatial variability in snowmelt timing
ggplot(usgs_discharge_doy, aes(x = doy_date, color = period, fill = period)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = discharge_min, ymax = discharge_max), 
              alpha = 0.4, lwd = 0) +
  geom_line(aes(y = discharge), lwd = 0.8) +
  # Add the period labels (Early: YYYY-YYYY / Late: YYYY-YYYY)
  geom_text(data = facet_labels, 
            aes(x = x_pos, y = y_pos, label = full_label),
            inherit.aes = FALSE,
            hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1.3, size = 2.8, lineheight = 0.9) +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "3 months", date_labels = "%b", expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_color_manual("Period", values = c("early" = pal$orange, "late" = pal$darkblue)) +
  scale_fill_manual("Period", values = c("early" = pal$orange, "late" = pal$darkblue)) +
  facet_wrap(~monitoring_location_name, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Historical Discharge Regimes: Early vs. Late Records",
       x = "Day of Year", 
       y = "Discharge (cfs)") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        strip.text = element_text(size = 7))

# Save the multi-gage comparison
ggsave("data/park/GLAC/Figs/usgs_discharge_regional.jpg", dpi = 600, width = 10, height = 7)

# --- 2. Focused 2025 Comparison (Swiftcurrent Creek) ---
# Restoration of the high-detail plot for the specific 2025 trend line
ggplot(usgs_discharge_doy %>% 
         filter(monitoring_location_name == "Swiftcurrent Creek at Many Glacier MT"), 
       aes(x = doy_date, color = period, fill = period)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = discharge_min, ymax = discharge_max), alpha = 0.4, lwd = 0) +
  geom_line(aes(y = discharge), lwd = 0.8) +
  # Overlay the 2025 data points/line
  geom_line(data = usgs_discharge_doy_2025 %>% 
              filter(monitoring_location_name == "Swiftcurrent Creek at Many Glacier MT"), 
            aes(x = doy_date, y = discharge, color = "2025"), lwd = 1) +
  geom_text(data = facet_labels %>% 
              filter(monitoring_location_name == "Swiftcurrent Creek at Many Glacier MT"), 
            aes(x = x_pos, y = y_pos, label = full_label),
            inherit.aes = FALSE,
            hjust = -0.2, vjust = 1.3, size = 3, lineheight = 0.9) +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b", expand = c(0, 0)) +
#  ylim(0,2000) +
  scale_color_manual("Period", values = c("2025" = "black", "early" = pal$orange, "late" = pal$darkblue)) +
  scale_fill_manual("Period", values = c("2025" = "black", "early" = pal$orange, "late" = pal$darkblue)) +
  labs(#title = "2025 Hydrological Comparison: Swiftcurrent Creek",
       x = "Day of Year", 
       y = "Discharge (cfs)") +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

ggsave("data/park/GLAC/Figs/usgs_discharge_2025_focus.jpg", dpi = 600, width = 7, height = 3)

```

#### ----- NWIS Groundwater

In this segment, we examine groundwater levels and hydrography. Monitoring groundwater elevation (NAVD88) and converting it to depth-to-water provides insight into the storage capacity and saturation levels of the aquifers supporting the park's water systems.

This chunk identifies nearby USGS monitoring wells, retrieves field-measured groundwater elevations, and calculates depth-to-water by comparing measurements against digital elevation points. It also retrieves high-resolution hydrography (NHDPlusHR) for the study area.

```{r nwis_gw}

# --- 1. Identify Groundwater Monitoring Wells ---
bbox_vals <- sf::st_bbox(park_boundary) %>%
  as.numeric() %>% 
  round(digits = 5)

# Filter for sites classified as "Well" within the park boundary
usgs_groundwater <- read_waterdata_monitoring_location(bbox = bbox_vals, site_type = "Well") %>%
  st_transform(crs = st_crs(park_boundary)) %>%
  st_filter(park_boundary) %>%
  # Ensure vertical datum is present for elevation-to-depth calculations
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(vertical_datum))

# --- 2. Retrieve Field Measurements ---
# Pull elevation data (62611 = GW elevation above datum) for the first five locations
usgs_groundwater_levels <- 
    dataRetrieval::read_waterdata_field_measurements(
      monitoring_location_id = usgs_groundwater$monitoring_location_id,
      parameter_code = "62611"
    ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    date = as.Date(time), 
    site_no = sub("USGS-", "", monitoring_location_id),
    ym = lubridate::ym(substr(date, 1, 7))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(year(date) >= 1900) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ym, monitoring_location_id) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    mean_lev = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(monitoring_location_id) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(dev_mean = mean_lev - mean(mean_lev, na.rm = TRUE),
                count = n()) %>%
  dplyr::filter(count > 1)

# --- 3. Elevation and Depth-to-Water Calculation ---
# Extract surface elevation at wellheads to calculate depth
usgs_groundwater <- usgs_groundwater %>%
  dplyr::filter(monitoring_location_id %in% unique(usgs_groundwater_levels$monitoring_location_id)) 

# Join datasets to calculate depth-to-water (Surface Elevation - Water Elevation)
usgs_groundwater_levels <- usgs_groundwater_levels %>%
  left_join(usgs_groundwater %>% st_drop_geometry() %>% 
              dplyr::select(monitoring_location_id, altitude), by = "monitoring_location_id") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(gw_depth_ft = altitude - mean_lev)

# --- 4. Visualization: Groundwater Depth Trends ---
colfunc <- colorRampPalette(c(c(pal$yellow,  pal$darkblue, pal$orange, pal$pink, pal$black)))
ggplot(usgs_groundwater_levels, 
       aes(x = ym, y = gw_depth_ft, col = monitoring_location_id)) + 
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) + 
  geom_line(alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_y_reverse() + # Standard convention: depth increases downward
  theme_bw() +
  labs(title = "Groundwater Depth Trends",
       x = "Year", 
       y = "Depth Below Surface (ft)") +
  scale_color_manual("", values = colfunc(nrow(usgs_groundwater)))


ggsave("data/park/GLAC/Figs/usgs_gw_depths_2025.jpg", dpi = 600, width = 6, height = 4)

```

### 4. Climate and Water Balance

In this section, we transition from historical observations to future climate projections. By leveraging the CMIP5 multi-model ensemble, we identify specific General Circulation Models (GCMs) that represent the diverging "Hot Dry" and "Warm Wet" climate futures for the Glacier National Park region.

#### - GCM Selection

This chunk filters regional climate model skill rankings and identifies the most divergent scenarios to bracket the range of potential hydrological impacts on park water supplies.

```{r}

# --- 3. Evaluate GCM Regional Skill ---
# Reference regional skill rankings for the Southwest Region (SWR)
all_cfs <- read_delim("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rossyndicate/CCRP_automated_climate_futures/master/data/general/GCM_skill_by_region.txt") %>%
  dplyr::filter(Region == "SWR") %>% 
  # Standardize naming conventions for HadGEM model variants
  dplyr::mutate(GCM = ifelse(GCM == "HadGEM2-ES.", "HadGEM2-ES365.", GCM),
                GCM = ifelse(GCM == "HadGEM2-CC.", "HadGEM2-CC365.", GCM)) %>%
  # Apply Representative Concentration Pathways (RCP 4.5 and 8.5)
  tidyr::crossing(data.table(RCP = c("rcp45", "rcp85"))) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(GCM = paste0(GCM, RCP),
                Skill = ifelse(Rank > 18, "Low Skill", "High Skill"))

```


#### - Download climate data

In this section, we acquire the high-resolution climate datasets necessary for driving the water balance models. This involves integrating historical GridMET data (4 km resolution) with future projections from the MACA (Multivariate Adaptive Constructed Analogs) downscaled GCMs, specifically subset to the Logan Pass recharge area.

This chunk defines the climate Area of Interest (AOI), visualizes the underlying data grid, and imports the pre-downloaded historical and future climate time series.

#### -  Run WBM

In this stage, we execute the National Park Service Water Balance Model (WBM) to translate raw meteorological inputs into hydrologically significant outputs such as snowpack accumulation, soil moisture, and actual evapotranspiration.

A key modification in this workflow is the calibration of the hock_coef to a value of 2. While the standard literature often defaults to 4, localized testing in high-elevation Western terrains has shown that a lower coefficient more accurately captures the snow accumulation and melt timing observed at SNOTEL sites.

The water balance model is adapted from code base developed in NPS's {WaterBalance} package (https://github.com/CCRP-Adaptation/WaterBalance). 

This chunk initializes the gridded soil and land cover rasters, runs the historical simulation to establish baseline conditions, and passes those "final state" values into the future projections to ensure a continuous hydrological record.

```{r wbm_run}

# --- 1. Parameterization and Initialization ---
# Load essential environmental rasters (AWC, Latitude, etc.) for the WBM
load_wbm_rasters(crs = crs(clim_pts))

# Calibrated Hock coefficient for snowmelt modeling
# Adjusted based on regional SNOTEL calibration (standard default is 4)

hock <- 3

# --- 2. Historical Baseline Run ---
# Run the WBM for each GridMET point to generate historical water budget components
recharge_wbm <- run_NPS_WBM_points(points = clim_pts,
                         climate_data = clim_hist,
                         #col_name = "GCM", # CSU ADDITION
                         Direct_Frac = 0, # CSU ADDITION
                         Return_Rate = 1, # CSU ADDITION
                         PET_Method = "Oudin",
                         hock_coef = hock,
                         Snowpack.Init = 0, 
                         Soil.Init = 0,
                         Shade.Coeff = 1,
                         T.Base = 0,
                         Soil_mult = 1,
                         PET_mult = 1,
                         ret_final_cond = TRUE,
                         area_weighted = FALSE, 
                         aoi = select_sources$watershed[[1]], 
                         grid = aoi_gridmet_grid,
                         aggregate = FALSE) 


# --- 3. Extract and Transfer Initial Conditions ---
# We use the final soil and snowpack levels from 2024 to prime the 2025 future runs
final_cond <- recharge_wbm[[2]] %>%
  dplyr::select(x,y,final_soil, final_snowpack)

clim_pts_fc <- clim_pts %>% 
  dplyr::left_join(final_cond, by = c("x","y"))

recharge_wbm <- recharge_wbm[[1]]

test_hock <- FALSE 

if (test_hock == TRUE) {

    ggplot(snotel_tidy %>%
               dplyr::filter(station_name == "Flattop Mtn.") %>%
               dplyr::select(date,wteq_i) %>%
               left_join(recharge_wbm %>%
                          dplyr::select(date, snowpack_in_wbm, x, y),
                         by = "date") %>%
              dplyr::filter(year(date) == 2020) %>%
              dplyr::group_by(date) %>%
            dplyr::mutate(mean_snowpack = mean(snowpack_in_wbm)),
       aes(x = date)) +
       geom_line(aes(y = snowpack_in_wbm, 
                  color = "WBM GRID", 
                  group = paste0(x,y)), lwd = 1) +
      geom_line(aes(y = mean_snowpack, color = "WBM MEAN"), lwd = 1) +
      geom_line(aes(y = wteq_i, color = "SNOTEL"), lwd = 1) +
      labs(x = "", y = "Snowpack (in)") +
      annotate("text", label = paste0("Hock Coef: ", hock), y = Inf, x = -Inf, 
               hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.5) +
      theme_bw() +
      scale_color_manual("", values = c("black","lightblue", "red"))

    ggsave(paste0("data/park/GLAC/Figs/Hock_",hock,".jpg"), width = 5, height = 3, dpi = 600)

}
  
# --- 4. Future Projection Run ---
# Execute the WBM for MACA climate futures (2025-2100)
recharge_fut_wbm <- run_NPS_WBM_points(points = clim_pts_fc,
                         climate_data = clim_fut,
                         #col_name = "GCM", # CSU ADDITION
                         Direct_Frac = 0, # CSU ADDITION
                         Return_Rate = 1, # CSU ADDITION
                         PET_Method = "Oudin",
                         hock_coef = hock,
                         Snowpack.Init = 0, 
                         Soil.Init = 0,
                         Shade.Coeff = 1,
                         T.Base = 0,
                         Soil_mult = 2,
                         PET_mult = 1,
                         ret_final_cond = FALSE,
                         use_final = FALSE,
                         area_weighted = FALSE, 
                         aoi = select_sources$watershed[[1]], 
                         grid = aoi_gridmet_grid,
                         aggregate = FALSE) 


rm(clim_fut, clim_hist, snotel_tidy)
gc()
```


#### - Routing

Apply routing function to runoff to better represent available supply. 

At Logan pass, water is sourced from snowmelt and precip runoff captured by an 
infiltration gallery along the slopes of Clements and Oberlin mountains. The WBM
runoff term represents all snowmelt and precip runoff that falls in the 
contributing (drainage) area for the infiltration gallery. However, in reality, 
a significant fraction of runoff is not captured by the infiltration gallery and
either a) exits the area from the nearby oberlin creek, b) flows past the 
infiltration area as shallow groundwater. The capacity of the infiltration
gallery and downstream water use from the tank both likely influence the amount
captured - therefore it is not expected to be a simple fraction of runoff.

In this section we:

a) apply a scaling factor to runoff to better match the total volume of water
captured by the infiltration gallery, and

b) apply a runoff routing function to better reflect the continuous nature
of surface and groundwater flow into the infiltration gallery as compared to
the temporally discontinuous signature of runoff.

```{r discharge}

# 1. Runoff Scaling (and data prep)

# This is a scale factor - modeled runoff is multiplied by this value to 
# better match the volume of water captured by the infiltration gallery.
# This value was tested across a range from 0.005 to 0.9 -
# any value above 0.05 is cleary WAY to much water
runoff_scale <- 0.025

# prepare temporary subset of data to test runoff scale and routing
mod_dat <- recharge_wbm %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(date) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(runoff_in_wbm = mean(runoff_in_wbm)) %>%
  # Keep only years that overlap with Logan Pass station data
  dplyr::filter(year(date) %in% unique(year(logan_sd$date))) %>%
  # Convert runoff depths to volumes (Cubic feet -> Gallons)
  dplyr::mutate(
    runoff_gal = runoff_scale * cf_to_gal * (runoff_in_wbm / 12) * recharge_area_ft2) %>%
  dplyr::select(date, runoff_gal) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  # Merge with supply data and apply a 7-day centered rolling mean to smooth noise
  dplyr::left_join(logan_sd, by = "date") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    supply_gal = frollmean(supply_gal, n = 7, align = "center", fill = mean(supply_gal))
  )

cal_dat <- mod_dat %>%
  dplyr::filter(year(date) %in% c(2016))


# 2. MANUAL MODEL CALIBRATION (Visual Check)

# Routing Parameters
tau_q <- 30 
tau_s <- 190
vs <- 0.2

# Run routing model with manual trial parameters
inflow_manual <- runoff_routing_gw(
  df                = mod_dat, 
  runoff_col        = "runoff_gal",
  date_col          = "date",
  tau_q             = tau_q, 
  tau_s             = tau_s, 
  vs                = vs,
  slow_only         = FALSE,
  return_components = TRUE,
  max_inf           = 5000
) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(mod_dat %>% dplyr::select(date, supply_gal, use_gal, runoff_gal), by = "date")




# Visual comparison of manual fit
peak_dates <- inflow_manual %>%
  dplyr::filter(month(date) %in% 6:9) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(year = year(date)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(Q_tot == max(Q_tot, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  dplyr::select(date, year) %>%
  dplyr::slice(1) # Ensure only one peak per year if there's a tie

ggplot(inflow_manual %>% 
         dplyr::filter(month(date) %in% 6:9) %>%
         dplyr::mutate(year = year(date)), 
       aes(x = date)) +
  # Vertical line for peak discharge (placed in background)
  geom_vline(data = peak_dates, aes(xintercept = date, group = year), 
             color = pal$darkblue, lwd = 0.5, linetype = "dashed") +
  # Reported Use
  geom_point(aes(y = use_gal, color = "Reported Use"), 
            linetype = "dashed", size = 0.5, alpha = 0.7) +
  # Reported Supply
  geom_point(aes(y = supply_gal, color = "Reported Supply"), 
            size = 0.6, alpha = 0.5) +
  
  # Modeled Components
  geom_line(aes(y = runoff_gal, color = "WBM"), 
            size = 0.7, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Q_tot, color = "WBM + Routing"), 
            size = 0.9) +

  facet_wrap(~year, scales = "free", ncol = 2) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_comma(), 
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%b", date_breaks = "1 month") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Reported Supply"     = "#000000", # Black
                                "WBM + Routing" = pal$darkblue, # Deep Blue
                                "WBM"    = pal$lightblue, # Vermillion/Orange
                                "Reported Use"           = "red"  # Grey
)) +
  
  # Styling
  theme_bw(base_size = 11, base_family = "sans") +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", color = NA),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = 11),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, color = "grey30"),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = "grey80", fill = NA)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Comparison of Modeled and Observed Supply",
    subtitle = "June – September System Dynamics",
    y = "Flow (Gallons per Day)"
  )



```

##### - Select CFS

Although we select a subset of GCMs that bound the range of uncertainty at Glacier. In this case, we start by selecting scenarios representing "hot dry", "warm dry", "hot wet", and "warm wet" climate futures. We then evaluate recharge projections for those futures and determine which to use as endmembers.

First calculate 30-year differentials (future - baseline) for all climate & WBM data stats

```{r}

# wbm_all 
wbm_all <- recharge_wbm %>%
  bind_rows(recharge_fut_wbm %>%
          dplyr::filter(year(date) > 2025)) %>%
  as.data.table() %>%
  left_join(all_cfs, by = "GCM") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(CF = ifelse(GCM == "GridMET", "GridMET", CF))

rm("recharge_fut_wbm", "recharge_wbm")
gc()


# Calculate stats for cf selection
all_clim_stats <- wbm_all %>%
  data.table() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    year = year(date),
    stat_period = case_when(
      year >= hist_yrs[[1]] & year <= hist_yrs[[2]] ~ "Baseline",
      year >= fut_yrs[[1]] & year < fut_yrs[[2]] ~ "Future", 
      TRUE ~ "Other")) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!stat_period == "Other") %>%
  dplyr::select(GCM, stat_period, Skill, precip_in_wbm, tmean_C, runoff_in_wbm, pet_in_wbm) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(GCM, stat_period, Skill) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(mean_precip_in = 365.25 * mean(precip_in_wbm),
                   mean_tmean_C = mean(tmean_C),
                   mean_runoff_in = 365.25 * mean(runoff_in_wbm),
                   median_runoff_in = quantile(runoff_in_wbm, 0.75),
                   sd_runoff_in = sd(runoff_in_wbm),
                   cv_runoff_in = sd(runoff_in_wbm)/mean(runoff_in_wbm),
                   iqr_runoff_in = as.numeric(quantile(runoff_in_wbm, 0.75)) - 
                     as.numeric(quantile(runoff_in_wbm, 0.25)),
                   q90_q10_runoff_in = as.numeric(quantile(runoff_in_wbm, 0.9)) -
                     as.numeric(quantile(runoff_in_wbm, 0.1)),
                   peak_runoff_in = max(runoff_in_wbm),
                   mean_precip_minus_pet_in = mean(precip_in_wbm - pet_in_wbm),
                   fract_zero_runoff = sum(runoff_in_wbm == 0) / n() ,
                   .groups = "keep") 

baseline <- all_clim_stats %>%
  dplyr::filter(stat_period == "Baseline")

future <- all_clim_stats %>%
  dplyr::filter(!stat_period == "Baseline")

future_differentials <- future %>%
  dplyr::mutate(delta_precip_in = mean_precip_in - baseline$mean_precip_in,
                delta_tmean_C = mean_tmean_C - baseline$mean_tmean_C,
                delta_runoff_in = mean_runoff_in - baseline$mean_runoff_in,
                delta_runoff_per = 100* (mean_runoff_in - baseline$mean_runoff_in)/baseline$mean_runoff_in,
                delta_precip_per = 100 * (mean_precip_in - baseline$mean_precip_in)/baseline$mean_precip_in,
                delta_runoff_in_sd = sd_runoff_in - baseline$sd_runoff_in,
                delta_runoff_in_cv = cv_runoff_in - baseline$cv_runoff_in,
                delta_runoff_in_iqr = iqr_runoff_in - baseline$iqr_runoff_in,
                delta_runoff_in_median = median_runoff_in - baseline$median_runoff_in,
                delta_runoff_q90_q10 = q90_q10_runoff_in - baseline$q90_q10_runoff_in,
                delta_runoff_in_peak = peak_runoff_in - baseline$peak_runoff_in,
                delta_precip_minus_pet = mean_precip_minus_pet_in - baseline$mean_precip_minus_pet_in,
                delta_fract_zero_runoff = fract_zero_runoff - baseline$fract_zero_runoff) %>%
  #dplyr::left_join(centroid_cfs %>% dplyr::select(GCM, CF), by = "GCM") %>%
  #dplyr::rename(c("centroid_cf" = CF)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(centroid_cf = ifelse(Skill == "Low Skill", "Low Skill", "Other")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(RCP = str_sub(GCM, -5))
```

##### - Aggregate WBM

Now, we're going to move forward without unselect climate future scenarios.

```{r Subset_WBM}
# Subset wbm for only selected CFs and grid cells

wbm <- wbm_all %>%
  data.table() %>%
  select(-c(Rank, Region, Skill, RCP, x, y, excess_water_in_wbm)) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(selected_gcms[[1]] %>% 
                     dplyr::filter(CF %in% c("Hot Dry", "Warm Wet")) %>%
                     dplyr::select(CF, GCM), 
                   by = "GCM") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(CF = ifelse(GCM == "GridMET", "Historical", CF)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(CF),
                year(date) > 1979) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(date,CF,GCM) %>%
  # Because we still have multiple grid cells, here we summarize with mean
  # of the AOI.
  dplyr::summarize(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)), 
                   .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(tmean_F = (9/5 * tmean_C) + 32) %>%
  # mult by recharge area to get volumes (Cubic feet and gallons)
  dplyr::mutate(runoff_cf = runoff_scale * (runoff_in_wbm / 12) * recharge_area_ft2, 
                runoff_gal = runoff_cf * cf_to_gal) # convert to gal

rm(wbm_all) 
gc()

# Add routing to main WBM
wbm <- wbm %>%
   dplyr::group_by(GCM) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(runoff_gal_low = 0.5 * runoff_gal,
                runoff_gal_high = 1.5 * runoff_gal) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(inflow_gal = runoff_routing_gw(
                                    df = data.table(date,runoff_gal), 
                                    runoff_col = "runoff_gal",
                                    date_col = "date",
                                    tau_q = tau_q,
                                    tau_s = tau_s,
                                    vs = vs,
                                    loss = 0,
                                    baseflow = 0,
                                    delay = 0,
                                    slow_only = TRUE,
                                    return_components = FALSE,
                                    max_inf = 5000
                                  )[,2],
                inflow_gal_low = runoff_routing_gw(
                                    df = data.table(date,runoff_gal_low),  # The .SD is the subset for the current group
                                    runoff_col = "runoff_gal_low",
                                    date_col = "date",
                                    tau_q = tau_q,
                                    tau_s = tau_s,
                                    vs = vs,
                                    loss = 0,
                                    baseflow = 0,
                                    delay = 0,
                                    slow_only = TRUE,
                                    return_components = FALSE,
                                    max_inf = 5000
                                  )[,2],
                inflow_gal_high = runoff_routing_gw(
                                    df = data.table(date,runoff_gal_high),  # The .SD is the subset for the current group
                                    runoff_col = "runoff_gal_high",
                                    date_col = "date",
                                    tau_q = tau_q,
                                    tau_s = tau_s,
                                    vs = vs,
                                    loss = 0,
                                    baseflow = 0,
                                    delay = 0,
                                    slow_only = TRUE,
                                    return_components = FALSE,
                                    max_inf = 5000
                                  )[,2]) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(inflow_cf = inflow_gal * gal_to_cf,
                inflow_cf_low = inflow_gal_low * gal_to_cf,
                inflow_cf_high = inflow_gal_high * gal_to_cf)


# Now, for temporal aggregation, some variables require mean, other's sum,
# and for snowpack, we'll look at the maximum annual snowpack.
mean_cols <- c("soil_in_wbm", "tmean_C", "tmean_F")
sum_cols <- c("precip_in_wbm", "runoff_in_wbm", "rain_in_wbm",
              "snow_in_wbm", "melt_in_wbm", "aet_in_wbm", "pet_in_wbm",
              "runoff_cf", "runoff_gal", "inflow_gal", "inflow_gal_low", "inflow_gal_high",
              "inflow_cf")
max_cols <- c("snowpack_in_wbm")

wbm_annual <- wbm %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year = year(date),
                month = month(date)) %>%
                #year = calc_water_year(date)) %>%
  dplyr::select(-date) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(year,GCM,CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    inflow_open_months_gal = sum(inflow_gal[month %in% 6:9], na.rm = TRUE),
    # Summarize specific columns with sum()
    across(all_of(mean_cols), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    # Summarize all other columns with mean()
    across(all_of(sum_cols), \(x) sum(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    across(all_of(max_cols), \(x) max(x, na.rm = TRUE))
  )

wbm_monthly <- wbm %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ym = make_ym(date)) %>%
  dplyr::select(-date) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ym, GCM, CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    # Summarize specific columns with sum()
    across(all_of(mean_cols), \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    # Summarize all other columns with mean()
    across(all_of(sum_cols), \(x) sum(x, na.rm = TRUE)),
    across(all_of(max_cols), \(x) max(x, na.rm = TRUE))
  )

# Percentage Changes
wbm_stats <- wbm_annual %>%
  dplyr::filter(year < 2013 | (year > 2034 & year < 2065)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(tmean_F = mean(tmean_F),
                   precip_in = mean(precip_in_wbm),
                   rain_in = mean(rain_in_wbm),
                   snow_in = mean(snow_in_wbm),
                   melt_in = mean(melt_in_wbm),
                   aet_in = mean(aet_in_wbm),
                   pet_in = mean(pet_in_wbm),
                   runoff_in = mean(runoff_in_wbm),
                   inflow_gal = mean(inflow_gal),
                   inflow_open_months_gal = mean(inflow_open_months_gal)) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), 
                ~ (. - .[CF == "Historical"]) / .[CF == "Historical"] * 100)) %>%
  filter(CF != "Historical")

print(wbm_stats)
```

```{r snotel_figs}
# Clean up snotel and weather station data to compare to gridmet/WBM
plot_dat <- weather_data_an %>%
  dplyr::filter(id %in% select_station_list,
                waterYear > 1983,
                waterYear < 2025) %>%
  # 1. Standardize names: Variable_Source
  dplyr::select(-prcp, snwd) %>%
  dplyr::rename("Snow Depth (in)"   = snwd,
                "Max Temp (F)"      = tmax,
                "Min Temp (F)"      = tmin
                #"Precipitation (in)_SS" = prcp
                ) %>%
  left_join(snotel_annual %>%
              dplyr::select(-snwd) %>%
              dplyr::rename("SWE (in)"           = wteq,
                            "Precipitation (in)" = prec),
            #                "Snow Depth (in)_SS"    = snwd),
            by = c("waterYear" = "water_year", "name" = "station_name")) %>%
  bind_rows(wbm_annual %>%
      dplyr::ungroup() %>%
      dplyr::filter(year < 2026) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(waterYear = year) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(name = "Logan Pass AOI",
                    snowpack_in_wbm = snowpack_in_wbm) %>%
      dplyr::select(waterYear, name, precip_in_wbm, 
                    snowpack_in_wbm, snow_in_wbm) %>%
      dplyr::rename("Precipitation (in)" = precip_in_wbm,
                    "Snow Depth (in)" = snowpack_in_wbm,
                    "SWE (in)" = snow_in_wbm)) %>%
  # 2. Pivot: This creates a 'variable' column and a 'data_source' column
  pivot_longer(cols = c("Precipitation (in)",
                        "Snow Depth (in)",
                        "SWE (in)"),
               names_to = "variable",
               values_to = "vals") %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Site = factor(name,
                              levels = c("Flattop Mtn.",

  dplyr::filter(!grepl("(F)|Snow", variable))

# 4. Final Plot

  # Faceting by 'variable' now puts WS and SS on the same plot for Precip and Snow Depth
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free_y", nrow = 3) + 
  labs(y = "", x = "") + 
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", 
        legend.box = "vertical",
        legend.margin = margin(t = -20, b = 0, l = 0, r = 0))
```

####- Visitation

Here we pull in park visitation data reported by the NPS and located in NPS IRMA.

```{r}

# Load in historical visitation data

# Get historical monthly reported visitor information
all_vis <- getUnitVisitation(units = park, 
                              startYear = 1979, 
                              endYear = 2026) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ym = lubridate::ym(paste0(Year, "-", Month))) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(TotalVisitors = RecreationVisitors + NonRecreationVisitors) %>%
  dplyr::select(ym, TotalVisitors) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(TotalVisitors = ifelse(TotalVisitors == 0,NA, TotalVisitors),
                month = month(ym))

# sum of West Entrance, Saint Mary, and Camas visitors (three entrances leading
# to Going-to-the-Sun Road which is the only way to access Logan Pass).

logan_vis <- read_csv("data/park/GLAC/Visitation/GLAC.csv") %>%
  dplyr::filter(metric %in% c("Visitors To Many Glacier",
                              "Visitors Via West Entrance",
                              "Visitors To Camas")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ym = month_start) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ym) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(LoganVisitors = sum(this_month)) %>%
  dplyr::select(ym, LoganVisitors)

visitors <- logan_vis %>% 
  left_join(all_vis, by = "ym") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(month = as.numeric(month(ym))) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(TotalVisitors = ifelse(TotalVisitors == 0, NA, TotalVisitors))

# Summarize monthly NPS visitation to annual sum
visitors_an <- visitors %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year = year(ym)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(year) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(ym, month)) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(
    TotalVisitors = sum(TotalVisitors, na.rm = TRUE),
    LoganVisitors = sum(LoganVisitors, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(year > 1997) %>%
   dplyr::mutate(TotalVisitors = ifelse(TotalVisitors == 0, NA, TotalVisitors))

library(ggpubr)

# Ensure LoganVisitors is filtered to avoid log(0) errors if using stat_regline
ggplot(visitors_an %>% dplyr::filter(LoganVisitors > 0), aes(x = year)) +
  # 1. Trendlines (using geom_smooth for the visual lines)
  geom_smooth(aes(y = TotalVisitors), method = "lm", se = FALSE, 
              color = "black", linetype = "dashed", lwd = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(aes(y = LoganVisitors), method = "lm", se = FALSE, 
              color = pal$pink, linetype = "dashed", lwd = 0.5) +
  
  # 2. Equations (using color-coded text)
  # Total Visitors Equation (Black)
  stat_regline_equation(aes(y = TotalVisitors),
                        label.x = 2000, label.y = 3.2e6, 
                        color = "black", size = 3.5) +
  # Logan Pass Equation (Pink)
  stat_regline_equation(aes(y = LoganVisitors),
                        label.x = 2000, label.y = 2.8e6, 
                        color = pal$pink, size = 3.5) +
  
  # 3. Main Data Lines
  geom_line(aes(y = LoganVisitors), color = "black", lwd = 1.5) +
  geom_line(aes(y = LoganVisitors, color = "Logan Pass"), lwd = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = TotalVisitors, color = "Total"), lwd = 1.5) +
  
  # 4. Formatting & Labels
  theme_bw() +
  labs(caption = "Logan Pass visitors assumed equal to sum of West Entrance, Saint Mary,\nand Camas visitors (three entrances leading to Going-to-the-Sun Road \nwhich is the only way to access Logan Pass).",
       x = "", 
       y = "Annual Visitors") +
  theme(plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0),
        legend.position = "bottom",
          legend.margin = margin(t = -15, b = 0, l = 0, r = 0)) +
  scale_color_manual("", values = c("Logan Pass" = pal$pink, "Total" = "black")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(scale = 1e-6, suffix = "M"),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.15))) # Adds room for equations at top

ggsave("data/park/GLAC/Figs/annual_visitors.jpg", dpi = 600, width = 5, height = 3)

# Create table of monthly mean, max, min, sd, and cv of historical visitors
monthly_visitor_proportions <- visitors %>%
          dplyr::mutate(year = year(ym)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(year != 2020) %>%
           dplyr::group_by(month) %>%
           dplyr::summarize(TV_mean = mean(LoganVisitors, na.rm = TRUE),
                            TV_max = max(LoganVisitors, na.rm = TRUE),
                            TV_min = min(LoganVisitors, na.rm = TRUE),
                            TV_sd = sd(LoganVisitors, na.rm = TRUE),
                            TV_cv = TV_sd / TV_mean) %>%
           dplyr::mutate(month_date = as_date(paste0("2000-",month,"-01")),
                         fraction = TV_mean/sum(TV_mean))

# Plot visitors to look at trends
ggarrange(
  ggplot(visitors_an %>% dplyr::filter(year != 2020), aes(x = year, y = LoganVisitors)) +
    geom_point(data = visitors_an %>% dplyr::filter(year == 2020), aes(x = year, y = LoganVisitors), color = "red") + 
    geom_line(data = visitors_an, aes(x = year, y = LoganVisitors), color = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_line() +
    geom_point() +
    
    geom_smooth() +
    labs(y = "Annual Total Visitors") +
    theme_bw(),
  ggplot(monthly_visitor_proportions, aes(x = month, y = TV_mean)) +
    geom_line() +
    geom_point() +
    labs(y = "Monthly Mean Total Visitors") +
    theme_bw())
```

Now, we'll develop a model to estimate future visitation. We'll develop a couple of models and select the one that performs best. National Park visitation has a complex set of drivers, many which we are beyond our ability to forecast. Here, we account for two major drivers of visitation: overall population increase and weather. 

For this first part, we develop a logistic model simply to account for visitor growth at the park. We assume some visitor carrying capacity for Logan Pass. This is unknown and could change in the future. Given recent population growth variability, we assume the carrying capacity is 5 million visitors per year.

```{r logistic}
# 1. Define an estimated Carrying Capacity (K) for CEBR
# We don't know what this value is, so we'll test a low, medium, and high value
K_limit_high <- 4500000
K_limit_low <- K_limit_high * 0.7
K_limit_mid <- K_limit_high * 0.8


logistic_mod <- function(K_limit, r, t0, year) {
  K_limit / (1 + exp(-r * (year - t0)))
}

fit_vis_logistic <- function(K_limit, df) {
  vis_mod_logistic <- nls(LoganVisitors ~ logistic_mod(K_limit, r, t0, year),#K_limit / (1 + exp(-r * (year - t0))),
                        data = df,
                        start = list(r = 0.05, t0 = 2010))
}


# 2. Fit a Logistic Model using Non-linear Least Squares
# This estimates 'r' (growth rate) and 't0' (the inflection point year)
vis_logistic_low <- fit_vis_logistic(K_limit_low, visitors_an %>% dplyr::filter(year != 2020))
vis_logistic_mid <- fit_vis_logistic(K_limit_mid, visitors_an %>% dplyr::filter(year != 2020))
vis_logistic_high <- fit_vis_logistic(K_limit_high, visitors_an %>% dplyr::filter(year != 2020))


# 3. Predict out to 2100
future_years <- data.frame(year = 1980:2100) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    pred_vis_low = predict(vis_logistic_low, newdata = .),
    pred_vis_mid = predict(vis_logistic_mid, newdata = .),
    pred_vis_high = predict(vis_logistic_high, newdata = .))

ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = visitors_an, aes(x = year, y = LoganVisitors, color = "Obs.")) +
  geom_ribbon(data = future_years, aes(x = year, ymin = pred_vis_low, ymax = pred_vis_high), alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(data = future_years, aes(x = year, y = pred_vis_mid, color = "mod")) +
  theme_bw() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = K_limit_mid, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "", y = "Total Visitors", title = "Simple Logistic Model to enforce visitor ceiling") +
  scale_color_manual("", values = c("black","red"))

```

Create annual visitation model

```{r annual_vis_model}

# 1. Finalize the annual data preparation
vis_mod_dat <- visitors_an %>%
  left_join(wbm_annual %>%
              dplyr::filter(year < 2026),
            by = "year") %>%
  dplyr::arrange(year) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(pop = logistic_mod(K_limit_mid, 
                                   coef(vis_logistic_mid)["r"],
                                   coef(vis_logistic_mid)["t0"],
                                   year),
                tmean_F_prev = dplyr::lag(tmean_F, 1),)

# 2. Fit the Annual GAM
vis_mod <- mgcv::gam(LoganVisitors ~ 
                       tmean_F +
                       #rain_in_wbm +
                       #snow_in_wbm +
                       snowpack_in_wbm +
                       pop, 
                     data = vis_mod_dat)

# 3. Generate Predictions and Residuals
vis_mod_dat <- vis_mod_dat %>%
  dplyr::filter(year > 1997) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(pred_vis = predict(vis_mod, newdata = .),
                # Ensure no negative visitors
                pred_vis = ifelse(pred_vis < 0, 0, pred_vis),
                pred_vis_residual = LoganVisitors - pred_vis)

# 4. Extract Model Performance Stats
r2_val <- round(summary(vis_mod)$r.sq, 2)
p_val <- format.pval(mean(summary(vis_mod)$p.pv), digits = 2, eps = 0.001)


# Create the multi-panel visualization
annual_vis_mod_plot <- ggarrange(
  # Panel A: Time Series (Observed vs Modeled)
  ggplot(vis_mod_dat) +
    geom_line(aes(x = year, y = LoganVisitors, color = "Observed"), size = 1) +
    geom_line(aes(x = year, y = pred_vis, color = "Modeled"), size = 1) +
    theme_bw() + 
    annotate("text", 
             label = as.character(as.expression(bquote(R^2 == .(r2_val) ~~~ p < .(p_val)))),
             parse = TRUE,
             x = -Inf, y = Inf, 
             hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.5,
             size = 4, fontface = "italic") +
    labs(x = "Year", y = "Annual Visitors", title = "Annual Model Performance") +
    scale_color_manual("", values = c("Modeled" = "tomato", "Observed" = "black")),

  # Panel B: Residuals over Time
  ggplot(vis_mod_dat, aes(x = year, y = pred_vis_residual)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
    geom_line() +
    geom_point() +
    labs(y = "Residual (# visitors)", x = "Year", title = "Annual Residuals") +
    theme_bw(),

  # Panel C: Observed vs Modeled (1:1 Plot)
  ggplot(vis_mod_dat, aes(x = LoganVisitors, y = pred_vis)) +
    geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, color = "black", linetype = "dotted", size = 1) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +
    theme_bw() +
    coord_equal() + # Important for 1:1 plots
    labs(x = "Observed Annual Visitors", y = "Modeled Annual Visitors", title = "1:1 Accuracy"),

  ncol = 1, # Stacked vertically to better see annual trends
  align = "v"
)

annual_vis_mod_plot
```

Now, use model to project visitation

```{r proj_vis}

# Prep future climate dataset and use model to project future visitation
vis_clim <- wbm_annual %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(pop = logistic_mod(K_limit_mid, 
                                   coef(vis_logistic_mid)["r"],
                                   coef(vis_logistic_mid)["t0"],
                                   year)) %>%
  dplyr::select(year, pop, tmean_F, GCM, CF, snowpack_in_wbm) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(GCM, CF) %>%
  dplyr::group_modify(~ {
    preds <- predict(vis_mod, newdata = .x, se.fit = TRUE)
    .x %>% mutate(vis_pred = as.numeric(preds$fit), 
                  vis_pred_SE = as.numeric(preds$se.fit))
  }) %>%
  #group_by(GCM, CF) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(vis_pred_low = vis_pred - (vis_pred_SE * 1.96),
                vis_pred_high = vis_pred + (vis_pred_SE * 1.96)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::group_by(year) %>%
  mutate(vis_yearly_max = max(vis_pred_high),
          vis_yearly_min = min(vis_pred_low),
          vis_yearly_mean = mean(c(vis_pred_high,vis_pred_low), na.rm = TRUE))

# View GAM model with predictions. Note, jagged bounds.
ggplot(vis_clim, aes(x = year, fill = CF, color = CF)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = vis_pred)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = vis_pred_low, ymax = vis_pred_high), alpha = 0.3, lwd = 0) +
  geom_point(data = visitors_an %>%
               dplyr::filter(year > 1997) %>%
               dplyr::mutate(CF = "Observed"),
             aes(x = year, y = LoganVisitors)) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "", y = "Annual Visitors") +
  scale_color_manual("", 
                       values = c(nps_pal$red, nps_pal$grey, "black", nps_pal$blue)) +
  scale_fill_manual("", values = c(nps_pal$red, nps_pal$grey, "black", nps_pal$blue))

# Because the GAM model predicts year-to-year estimates that vary with temp,
# we then calculate a smooth model from the predictions for plots.
# Re-fit like above butfind the best r and t0 for these specific bounds
# Note: We keep K_limit fixed based on your previous 'mid' assumption
fit_smooth_logistic <- function(y_var, df, K) {
  nls(y_var ~ logistic_mod(K, r, t0, year), 
      data = df, 
      start = list(r = 0.05, t0 = 2050))
}

# Apply the fits
# (Using the mid K_limit you defined earlier)
log_mod_proj <- fit_smooth_logistic(vis_clim$vis_yearly_mean, vis_clim, max(vis_clim$vis_yearly_mean))
log_mod_high <- fit_smooth_logistic(vis_clim$vis_yearly_max, vis_clim, max(vis_clim$vis_yearly_max))
log_mod_low  <- fit_smooth_logistic(vis_clim$vis_yearly_min, vis_clim, max(vis_clim$vis_yearly_min))

# 3. Add the smooth lines back to the dataframe for plotting
vis_clim <- vis_clim %>%
  ungroup() %>% # Ensure no groups are interfering
  mutate(
    # predict() here will now correctly return 197 values for the 197 rows
    vis_smooth_mid  = as.numeric(predict(log_mod_proj, newdata = .)),
    vis_smooth_high = as.numeric(predict(log_mod_high, newdata = .)),
    vis_smooth_low  = as.numeric(predict(log_mod_low, newdata = .))
  ) %>%
  left_join(visitors_an %>% dplyr::select(year, LoganVisitors), by = "year")

# Now view smooth plot
ggplot(vis_clim, aes(x = year, fill = CF, color = CF)) +
   geom_point(aes(y = vis_pred)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = vis_pred_low, ymax = vis_pred_high), alpha = 0.3, lwd = 0) +
  geom_point(data = visitors_an %>%
               dplyr::mutate(CF = "Observed"),
             aes(x = year, y = LoganVisitors)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = vis_smooth_mid)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = vis_smooth_low, ymax = vis_smooth_high), alpha = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(data = visitors_an %>%
               dplyr::mutate(CF = "Observed"),
             aes(x = year, y = LoganVisitors)) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "", y = "Annual Visitors") +
  scale_color_manual("", 
                       values = c(nps_pal$red, nps_pal$grey, "black", nps_pal$blue)) +
  scale_fill_manual("", values = c(nps_pal$red, nps_pal$grey, "black", nps_pal$blue))

# Monthly vis
proj_vis_sum <- vis_clim %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::filter(year > 2034, year < 2065) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(mean_vis = mean(vis_smooth_mid),
                   max_vis = max(vis_smooth_high),
                   min_vis = min(vis_smooth_low)) 


# Monthly visitor proportions - projections 
monthly_visitor_proportions <- monthly_visitor_proportions %>%
  dplyr::mutate(fut_min_vis = proj_vis_sum$min_vis * fraction,
                fut_max_vis = proj_vis_sum$max_vis * fraction,
                fut_mean_vis = proj_vis_sum$mean_vis * fraction)

# Monthly visitors
monthly_visitors <- vis_clim %>%
 full_join(data.frame(ym = seq.Date(from = as.Date("1979-01-01"), 
                                    to = as.Date("2099-12-01"), by = "month")) %>%
                      dplyr::mutate(year = year(ym)), by = "year") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(ym) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(vis_smooth_mid = mean(vis_smooth_mid, na.rm = TRUE),
                   vis_smooth_low = min(vis_smooth_low, na.rm = TRUE),
                   vis_smooth_high = max(vis_smooth_high, na.rm = TRUE),
                   LoganVisitors = mean(LoganVisitors, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(month = month(ym),
                year = year(ym)) %>%
  left_join(monthly_visitor_proportions %>%
              dplyr::select(month, fraction), by = "month") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(monthly_vis = ifelse(year < 2025, 
                                     fraction * LoganVisitors, 
                                     fraction * vis_smooth_mid),
                monthly_vis_high = ifelse(year < 2025, 
                                          fraction * LoganVisitors, 
                                          fraction * vis_smooth_high),
                monthly_vis_low = ifelse(year < 2025, 
                                         fraction * LoganVisitors, 
                                         fraction * vis_smooth_low)) %>%
  dplyr::select(ym, monthly_vis_low, monthly_vis_high, monthly_vis)
```

#### - Water use

We estimate water use based on visitation with low, mid, and high use per visitor estimates based on published values.

```{r water_use}

# Therefore, we'll estimate based on visitation

#    0.566       0.390      0.187

high_use_per_visitor <- .5 * gal_to_cf # --> equal to 5 gallons [high range use]
low_use_per_visitor <- 0.3 * gal_to_cf # Past use rate (hughes, 1996) [low use]
mid_use_per_visitor <- 0.4 * gal_to_cf # # [mid range use]

# Calculate monthly use proportions (NOTE THESE ARE IN CF)
monthly_use_proportions <- monthly_visitor_proportions %>%
  dplyr::select(month, month_date, TV_mean, fut_mean_vis) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(mid_use_hist = TV_mean * mid_use_per_visitor,
                mid_use_fut = fut_mean_vis * mid_use_per_visitor,
                low_use_hist = TV_mean * low_use_per_visitor,
                low_use_fut = fut_mean_vis * low_use_per_visitor,
                high_use_hist = TV_mean * high_use_per_visitor,
                high_use_fut = fut_mean_vis * high_use_per_visitor,
                use_fraction = mid_use_hist / sum(mid_use_hist)) %>%
  # Assign 0 if visitor center closed
  dplyr::mutate(across(
    c(low_use_hist, mid_use_hist, high_use_hist, 
      low_use_fut, mid_use_fut, high_use_fut),
    ~ ifelse(month %in% c(10, 11, 12, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5), 0, .))) %>%
  dplyr::select(month, month_date, low_use_hist, mid_use_hist, 
                high_use_hist, low_use_fut, mid_use_fut, high_use_fut)


# Multiply annual by monthly use proportions
monthly_use <- monthly_visitors %>%
  dplyr::filter(year(ym) > 1997) %>%
  arrange(ym) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(month = month(ym)) %>%
  # 1. Calculate the use values
  dplyr::mutate(monthly_use_low = monthly_vis_low * low_use_per_visitor,
                monthly_use_mid = monthly_vis * mid_use_per_visitor,
                monthly_use_high = monthly_vis_high * high_use_per_visitor) %>%
  # 2. Keep 'month' here so 'across' can see it!
  dplyr::select(ym, month, monthly_use_low, monthly_use_high, monthly_use_mid) %>%
  # 3. Now run the seasonal mask
  dplyr::mutate(across(
    c(monthly_use_low, monthly_use_high, monthly_use_mid),
    ~ case_when(month %in% c(10, 11, 12, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5) ~ 0,
                month %in% c(6,9) ~ .*0.25,
                month %in% c(7,8) ~.))) %>%
  # 4. Join with WBM data
  left_join(logan_sd_monthly, by = "ym")




# Compare recorded and modeled monthly use:
ggplot(monthly_use %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(use_gal)), aes(x = ym)) +
  
  geom_line(aes(y = use_gal / 1000, color = "Recorded"),

  geom_point(aes(y = (monthly_use_mid * cf_to_gal) / 1000, color = "Modeled"),

  # Professional Styling

# Calculate annual use
annual_use <- monthly_use %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year = year(ym)) %>%

  dplyr::summarize(mid_use = sum(monthly_use_mid,na.rm = TRUE),
```

#####- Supply Calculate monthly supply and demand

```{r}


# --- 1. Calculate Monthly Supply Proportions ---
monthly_supply_proportions <- wbm %>%
  select(CF, date, runoff_cf) %>%
  mutate(ym = make_ym(date)) %>%
  # Aggregate to monthly total per Climate Future (CF) and Model (GCM)
  group_by(ym, CF) %>%
  summarize(runoff_cf = sum(runoff_cf, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(
    month = month(ym),
    year  = year(ym),
    group = case_when(
      year <= 2012 ~ "Historical",
      year > 2034 & year < 2065 ~ "Future",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  drop_na(group) %>%
  # Calculate summary stats per month and CF
  group_by(month, CF) %>%
  summarize(
    monthly_supply_cf     = mean(runoff_cf, na.rm = TRUE),
    monthly_supply_cf_max = max(runoff_cf, na.rm = TRUE),
    monthly_supply_cf_min = min(runoff_cf, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    month_date = as_date(paste0("2000-", month, "-01")),
    month_days = days_in_month(month_date)
  ) %>%
  # Calculate fractional distribution across the year
  group_by(CF) %>%
  mutate(
    total_cf         = sum(monthly_supply_cf),
    monthly_fraction = monthly_supply_cf / total_cf
  ) %>% 
  ungroup()

# --- 2. Process Monthly Demand (Long Format) ---
monthly_use_long <- monthly_use_proportions %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = matches("(mid|low|high)_use_(fut|hist)"), 
    names_to  = "use_cat", 
    values_to = "use_cf"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Offset dates for visualization separation
    month_date = case_when(
      grepl("hist", use_cat) ~ month_date - years(4),
      TRUE                   ~ month_date + years(50)
    ),
    new_group = case_when(
      grepl("low", use_cat)  ~ "low_use",
      grepl("high", use_cat) ~ "high_use",
      TRUE                   ~ "mid_use"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(month_date, new_group, use_cf) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = new_group, values_from = use_cf)

# --- 3. Demand-Supply (DS) Ratio Analysis ---
DS_df <- wbm_annual %>%
  select(year, CF, runoff_cf) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(runoff_cf = runoff_cf) %>%
  left_join(annual_use, by = "year") %>%
  mutate(
    DS             = mid_use / runoff_cf,
    DS_stress      = high_use / runoff_cf,
    DS_over_pt2    = if_else(DS >= 0.2, 1, 0),
    DS_over_1      = if_else(DS >= 1, 1, 0)
  )

# --- 4. Final Statistics ---
DS_stats <- DS_df %>%
  filter(
    (year >= 1980 & year <= 2012) | 
    (year >= 2035 & year <= 2064)
  ) %>%
  group_by(CF) %>%
  summarize(
    n                       = n(),
    high_stress_years       = 100 * sum(DS_over_pt2) / n,
    inadequate_supply_years = 100 * sum(DS_over_1) / n,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(DS_stats)

```


# 7. Drought (SPEI)

```{r spei}

# Calculate SPEI
# Calculate SPEI using the {spei} package

# This method allows control to summarize by 2 months or 6 months simply
# by changing ag_n to the aggregate #. 1 = monthly, 6 = 6 months.
ag_n <- 6 # number of months to aggregate for time series, 1 = monthly
freq <- 12/ag_n # frequency 
agg_months <- ifelse(ag_n == 1, paste0(ag_n, " month"), paste0(ag_n, " months"))

# Aggregate into ag_n dataframe
agg_wbm <- wbm %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::mutate(year = year(date),
                month = month(date),
                time_ag = floor_date(date, agg_months)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(year, time_ag, CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(precip_in_wbm = sum(precip_in_wbm, na.rm = TRUE),
                   tmean_C = mean(tmean_C, na.rm = TRUE),
                   pet_in_wbm = sum(pet_in_wbm, na.rm = TRUE),
                   runoff_in_wbm = sum(runoff_in_wbm, na.rm = TRUE),
                   runoff_gal = sum(runoff_gal, na.rm = TRUE),
                   snow_in_wbm = sum(snow_in_wbm, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(balance = precip_in_wbm - pet_in_wbm,
                month = month(time_ag)) %>% 
  ungroup()


# Grab last year of WBM data
end_year = agg_wbm$year %>% tail(n = 1)
end_month = agg_wbm$month %>% tail(n = 1)

# Calculate SPEI for Hot Dry and Warm Wet futures. Both require historical data
# so calculate separately then join
# Hot Dry
spei_hot_dry <- agg_wbm %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::filter(CF %in% c("Historical", "Hot Dry")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(spei = c(spei(ts(c(balance), 
                                         end = c(end_year, end_month), 
                                         frequency = freq),
                                      scale = freq,
                                      ref.end = c(2023, 1)) %>%
                                   .[["fitted"]])) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ym = as.Date(paste0(year,"-",month,"-01")))

# Warm Wet
spei_warm_wet <- agg_wbm %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::filter(CF %in% c("Historical", "Warm Wet")) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(spei = c(spei(ts(balance, 
                                          end = c(end_year, end_month), 
                                          frequency = freq), 
                           scale = freq,
                           ref.end = c(2023, 1)) %>%
                        .[["fitted"]])) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(ym = as.Date(paste0(year,"-",month,"-01")))

# Join
spei <- bind_rows(
  spei_hot_dry %>% dplyr::filter(year >= 2024),
  spei_warm_wet
)


# Calculate Drought Metrics from SPEI

#' 1. Frequency and Duration of Drought Events: Threshold-Based Identification: 
#' Define drought events based on crossing a specific negative SPEI threshold 
#' (e.g., SPEI < -1 for moderate drought, SPEI < -1.5 for severe drought, 
#' SPEI < -2 for extreme drought). Frequency: Calculate the number of drought 
#' events occurring within a defined historical period and within different 
#' projected future periods (e.g., 2021-2050, 2051-2080, 2081-2100). Compare the 
#' frequency between historical and future periods. Duration: For each 
#' identified drought event, calculate its duration (number of consecutive 
#' months below the threshold). Compare the average or maximum drought duration 
#' between historical and future periods. You can also analyze the distribution 
#' of drought durations.


# Drought severity
spei_severity <- spei %>%
  dplyr::filter(year < 2065) %>%
  drop_na(spei) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(moderate = spei <= -1,
                severe = spei <= -1.5,
                extreme = spei <= -2) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(n = n(),
                   mod_percent = 100*sum(moderate, na.rm = TRUE)/n,
                   sev_percent = 100*sum(severe, na.rm = TRUE)/n,
                   ext_percent = 100*sum(extreme, na.rm =TRUE)/n,
                   mean_spei = mean(spei),
                   median_spei = median(spei, na.rm = TRUE),
                   sd_spei = sd(spei, na.rm = TRUE))


# Drought frequency
spei_frequency <- spei %>%
  drop_na(spei) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(moderate = spei <= -1,
                severe = spei <= -1.5,
                extreme = spei <= -2) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(mod_event = cumsum(moderate & !lag(moderate, default = FALSE)),
                sev_event = cumsum(severe & !lag(severe, default = FALSE)),
                ext_event = cumsum(extreme & !lag(extreme, default = FALSE)))

spei_metrics <- left_join(
  spei_frequency %>% 
  dplyr::filter(moderate) %>%
  group_by(CF, mod_event) %>% 
  dplyr::summarize(start = min(ym),
                end = max(ym),
                duration = n(),
                mean_spei = mean(spei, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(mod_mean_duration = mean(duration, na.rm = TRUE)/freq,
                   mod_max_duration = max(duration, na.rm = TRUE)/freq,
                   mod_median_duration = median(duration, na.rm = TRUE)/freq,
                   mod_mean_spei = mean(mean_spei, na.rm = TRUE)),
  spei_frequency %>% 
  dplyr::filter(severe) %>%
  group_by(CF, sev_event) %>% 
  dplyr::summarize(start = min(ym),
                end = max(ym),
                duration = n(),
                mean_spei = mean(spei, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(sev_mean_duration = mean(duration, na.rm = TRUE)/freq,
                   sev_max_duration = max(duration, na.rm = TRUE)/freq,
                   sev_median_duration = median(duration, na.rm = TRUE)/freq,
                   sev_mean_spei = mean(mean_spei, na.rm = TRUE)), by = "CF") %>%
  left_join(
  spei_frequency %>% 
  dplyr::filter(extreme) %>%
  group_by(CF, ext_event) %>% 
  dplyr::summarize(start = min(ym),
                end = max(ym),
                duration = n(),
                mean_spei = mean(spei, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(CF) %>%
  dplyr::summarize(ext_mean_duration = mean(duration, na.rm = TRUE)/freq,
                   ext_max_duration = max(duration, na.rm = TRUE)/freq,
                   ext_median_duration = median(duration, na.rm = TRUE)/freq,
                   ext_mean_spei = mean(mean_spei, na.rm = TRUE)), by = "CF") %>%
  left_join(spei_severity, by = "CF") %>%
  t() %>%
  as.data.frame(stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  row_to_names(row_number = 1) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column(var = "Metric") %>%
  arrange(Metric)

# Alternative to consider later (thoughts)
#Transition Probabilities and Persistence: Markov Chain Analysis: Treat SPEI categories (e.g., non-drought, mild drought, moderate drought, etc.) as states in a Markov chain. Estimate the transition probabilities between these states based on the historical SPEI time series. Then, project future transition probabilities and compare them to the historical ones. An increase in the probability of transitioning to or staying in more severe drought categories indicates a higher risk of prolonged and intense drought. Analyze sequences of SPEI values below a certain threshold to identify drought "runs." Calculate the probability of a drought ending within a certain timeframe based on historical data and compare this to projections.



ggplot(spei %>% dplyr::filter(month(ym) == 7), aes(x = spei, y = snow_in_wbm)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_smooth(fill = "orange", color = "maroon", alpha = 0.2) +
  theme_bw() +
```
